caption: What if you slept in an igloo? On an Arctic winter night it can drop to about -45 °C outside, and all you have to build with is snow. The trick: snow is up to 95% trapped air, so it insulates like a thick razai. Blocks spiral up into a curved dome with no beams and no cement. The entrance tunnel is dug low so cold air sinks into it like a trap, while the sleeping platform is raised into the warmer air. With body heat alone, the inside can stay between -7 and 16 °C while it's -45 outside. A lamp melts the inner walls slightly, and they refreeze into a layer of ice that makes the igloo stronger. In 2022, Gulmarg in Kashmir opened an igloo café about 11.4 m tall with 40 seats. Plot twist: in Inuktitut, 'iglu' simply means house, any house. So technically, you already live in one. Would YOU spend a night in an igloo? 👇
